task: 2026-10-02 targeted fixes: (1) client numbers silently losing their client allocation, (2) Client Test Panel range filter showing nothing although the panel lists test numbers, (3) Test Panel added to the Agent panel
scope: Only these three issues. No changes to SMS receiving, HTTP/API behaviour, SMPP, providers, DB schema, users/roles/permissions, payments, rates, commission, CDR, reports, existing business rules, theme, sidebar layout or any other panel behaviour.

issue1_client_allocation_lost.symptom: A number that was allocated to a client later appears unallocated / disappears from that client's panel without the client doing anything.
issue1_client_allocation_lost.investigation: Audited the whole lifecycle on the isolated fixture: 173 API routes, all 24 UPDATE numbers sites, every timer (runRetentionSweep, providerSync, SMPP outbox, cleanupApiIntegrationTables, STATS-RECONCILE), DB triggers (only FTS), backend/backup.js, scripts/, ecosystem.config.js, exportWorker.js, the api-integration poller and every front-end call site. A Playwright sweep over every page of all four panels (178s) recorded 0 non-GET API calls and 0 ownership changes; a controlled allocate->monitor test (423s) showed no change in client_id. There is no scheduled/background/auto-release process for client ownership.
issue1_client_allocation_lost.root_cause: POST /api/numbers/allocate -> handleAllocate() (backend/server.js). The UPDATE it runs was only limited by the caller's hierarchy scope: `WHERE n.id IN (SELECT id FROM tmp_alloc_ids) AND (<scope>)`. The ownership guard documented in the comment right above it ('only unallocated numbers (or numbers already owned by this target) are assigned - silent ownership steal is impossible / Explicit force=true ... reassigns') was never in the SQL, and no panel ever sent force=true. Any allocate request whose id list contains numbers that already belong to a client therefore overwrote them: allocating to another client moved the numbers away from the first client, and allocating to a manager/agent tier (or a range/select-all that includes client rows) wrote client_id=NULL - i.e. the client's numbers became unallocated with no confirmation and no audit of a deliberate reassignment.
issue1_client_allocation_lost.fix: handleAllocate now only touches numbers that are unallocated at the target tier or already owned by that exact target, unless the caller explicitly sends force=true (the deliberate reassignment feature is preserved). The response additionally reports blocked / blocked_ids / blocked_sample so a UI can ask before reassigning. admin.html, manager.html, agent.html and management.html 'Allocate All' flows now show the real allocated count, ask for confirmation when numbers are already allocated to somebody else, and only then resend those ids with force=true.

issue2_client_test_panel_range_filter.symptom: Client Test Panel: the Range dropdown shows no options ('Not Available') although the panel below lists test numbers for those ranges.
issue2_client_test_panel_range_filter.root_cause: The Range filter of the client Test Panel was built from /api/ranges only. That route is ownership scoped for non-admins (P19f: only ranges in which the user holds numbers), while the Test Panel data itself (/api/test-numbers, /api/test-panel/sms) is the shared test-number pool. A client with no allocated numbers - or with numbers in only one range - therefore got an empty (or partial) filter while the panel was showing test numbers of ranges that never appeared in it.
issue2_client_test_panel_range_filter.fix: client.html: the Test Panel range list is now the union of the ranges the client owns (unchanged /api/ranges scope) and the ranges of the active test numbers the panel is already displaying (/api/test-numbers). No new endpoint, no server-side scope change and no permission widened; ranges that have neither the client's numbers nor test numbers stay unavailable. The agent Test Panel (issue 3) uses the same rule.

issue3_agent_test_panel.fix: agent.html: new top-level 'Test Panel' entry in the existing rail navigation (same icon/structure as the Manager/Client Test Panel, no sidebar redesign) plus a #page-test section that reuses the existing Test Panel endpoints (/api/test-numbers, /api/test-panel/sms), the existing range-filter logic and the existing agent masking rule (CLI masked, SMS body never shown - the same rule admin.html models as 'admin=full, agent=masked'). Read-only: the page performs no write call.
